profile_name: Regional Crime — Present-Tense Clock Open, Skeptical of the Official Story
based_on: A faceless English channel about crimes from one region of the United States (~4,300 words, 30 minutes, photos, real footage and some 2D animation). No names, places or cases from the original are kept.
best_for: a regional brand ('crimes of the Pacific Northwest', 'of the South', 'of one state'); cases with institutional failures, cover-ups or wrongful convictions; long 2–4 hour regional compilations

point_of_view.narration: third-person PRESENT tense in the opening scene, past tense afterwards
point_of_view.viewer_address: brand line at the start and after the hook; occasional 'well,' asides

audience_addressing_style: branded narrator: 'You're watching [CHANNEL NAME].' then 'This is [CHANNEL NAME].' after the hook

hook_style.type: date, time and place stamp, then a clock-driven scene
hook_style.formula: You're watching [CHANNEL NAME]. [City], [State], [full date]. It's a [weekday] evening, [exact time]. [Atmosphere: lights clicking off, early winter dark]. [Who the person is and why he mattered]. [He walks to his car, but he'll never drive away]. [Time stamps of who noticed what, and who failed to call]. [The discovery]. [The detail that contradicts the official explanation]. [Officials will call it X, but the facts suggest something darker]. This is [CHANNEL NAME].

narrative_structure.type: clock open → who the victim was and what he threatened → the official version → the witnesses and confessions that did not fit → how the system steered the case → the wrongful outcome → what is still unanswered
beats_in_order: 2. The victim's career and why powerful people had reasons to fear him.
4. Tips, sketches and witnesses that pointed elsewhere.
5. A confession containing a detail never made public, and why it was dismissed.
6. Pressure on witnesses, lost or shredded evidence, immunity deals.
7. The person convicted and why the evidence against him was thin.
9. The system described as a machine that absorbs scandal.
10. Closing image: the physical place of the crime and the distance that holds the mystery.

pacing.overall: brisk; each paragraph adds a new document, witness or contradiction
pacing.lists: stacked verbs for cover-up summaries ('absorb the murder, steer the investigation, pressure witnesses…')

sentence_style.mix: clean declaratives; ironic understatement ('Now, that alone should have been notable.')

language_style.evidence_words: documents, printouts, sketches, immunity, confession details withheld from the public

characters.victim: an insider who was about to expose something
characters.institutions: the real antagonist, described by documented actions
characters.the_convicted: possibly the wrong man; treated fairly

dialogue.use: documented quotes from confessions, prosecutors and reporters

emotional_tone.arc: quiet routine → shock → suspicion → frustration → unresolved unease

common_devices: branded opener and branded line after the hook
'Officials will call it X, but…' pivot
cover-up summarised as a list of verbs
closing on a physical distance or place

call_to_action_style.closing: none, or a single subscribe line

visual_cue_prompts.hook: 3D or stock of the building at night, lights turning off, car with the door open, clock overlays
visual_cue_prompts.documents: highlighted memos, sketches, shredded paper motif
visual_cue_prompts.regional_brand: regional map with the case pinned among earlier cases

safety_and_compliance: Separate documented facts from theories; label theories clearly.
Never accuse a named living person of a crime without a conviction or credible documented allegation.
Fair treatment of the convicted person and of officials.

script_formatting_rules.parts: The final script must be sectioned into 10 parts, each part at least 800 words.
script_formatting_rules.total_length: The full script must be 8,000+ words in total.
script_formatting_rules.no_headings: No section headings, no part numbers, no titles inside the text.
script_formatting_rules.no_line_breaks: No line breaks: the whole script is one continuous block of text.
script_formatting_rules.no_symbols: No underscores, no bullet points, no brackets, no stage directions, no visual cues, no comments.
script_formatting_rules.no_wrappers: No introductory statement and no closing statement outside the narration itself.
script_formatting_rules.delivery: Send the whole script in one batch, only the script text, with nothing before or after it.
